title: How the device tree is built in layers

steps.title: Four layers merge into one board file
steps.body:
A device tree is a text description of the hardware, and this board's is split into layers. Each layer describes only what it adds; later layers switch nodes on or change them through `&labels`.

Read the four columns left to right, then the result and the 47-file explanation below.

steps.title: Layer 1: the chip, with most things switched off
steps.body:
`imx8mp.dtsi` comes from NXP and is 2403 lines. It describes every block inside the i.MX 8M Plus: CPUs, GIC, clocks, I2C, uSDHC, Ethernet, GPU and VPU.

Most nodes are `status = "disabled"` (65 of them), because the chip alone cannot know which are wired to anything.

steps.title: Layer 2: what is soldered on the module
steps.body:
Variscite's 567-line `imx8mp-var-som.dtsi` adds the PMIC, eMMC, Ethernet PHY, Wi-Fi and the pin muxing for the module's own parts.

For example it sets `&usdhc3` to an 8-bit bus with `status = "okay"`: that is the eMMC.

steps.title: Layer 3: what the carrier board wires up
steps.body:
The carrier layer, 685 lines, enables the SD slot, GPIO expanders, RTC, touch, LVDS panel, CAN and audio. It turns on `&i2c4` and adds an `rtc@68` node with compatible `dallas,ds1337`.

This is the only layer you write for your own carrier board.

steps.title: Layer 4: an overlay for revision 1.x
steps.body:
A 29-line overlay (`.dtso`) captures the differences of SoM revision 1.x, such as an older Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip. It disables `&bluetooth_iw61x` and reconfigures `&usdhc1`.

It is applied after the others, not merged in the source.

steps.title: The Makefile merges them into one .dtb
steps.body:
`dtc` merges layers 1 to 3 into the base `.dtb`, then `fdtoverlay` applies layer 4. The result, `imx8mp-var-som-1.x-symphony.dtb`, is what the kernel sees.

The merge rule lives in the `Makefile` in `arch/arm64/boot/dts/freescale/`.

steps.title: 47 files because the options multiply
steps.body:
Module (dart, som, smarc), revision, carrier (sonata, symphony, echo), camera and M7 options combine, and each combination is a different board with its own DTB.

U-Boot's `findfdt` picks yours at boot, giving `fdt_file=imx8mp-var-som-1.x-symphony.dtb`.

steps.anchor: Rule of thumb: describe the chip once (SoC), the module once (SoM), and each carrier once. To support your own carrier board, you
steps.title: Takeaway: write only layer 3
steps.body:
Describe the chip once, the module once and each carrier once. For your own carrier, copy the Symphony `.dts` into `custom/dts/`, keep `#include "imx8mp-var-som.dtsi"`, and change what your board wires differently.

On the board, `ls /proc/device-tree` shows the result.
